days.title: Departure from Poland
days.tagline: Warsaw at midnight. Ten and a half hours over the Pole. Wake up in Japan.
highlights: 20:30 — Warsaw Chopin (WAW), check-in + security with a 2h buffer
22:50 — LO79 lifts off for Narita (~10h 30min over the polar route)
Powerbank, eye mask, snacks, change of clothes — all in the carry-on
Set watches to JST when boarding. Try to sleep before midnight CET.
days.food: Light dinner at WAW. LOT serves a meal in-flight — pack snacks just in case.
days.tip: Tokyo is 7h ahead and you land mid-afternoon. Hydrate, walk the aisle every couple of hours, sleep when you can.

days.title: Tokyo Arrival — the lost day
days.tagline: Land at Narita. N'EX to Shinjuku. First konbini run. Sleep before midnight.
highlights: 16:20 — Land at NRT (immigration 30–45 min)
17:30 — Narita Express to Shinjuku (~80 min, ¥3,070)
19:30 — Check into lyf Shinjuku, drop bags
20:30 — First konbini run (7-Eleven onigiri are vegan-friendly)
22:00 — Sleep. Tomorrow is teamLab.
days.food: Konbini onigiri (umeboshi, kombu fillings are naturally GF + vegan). 7-Eleven and Lawson have labelled vegan onigiri.
days.tip: Withdraw yen at 7-Eleven ATMs — best rates, English menus. Buy a Suica IC card at the airport kiosk on arrival.

days.title: TeamLab Borderless · Shinjuku · Shibuya
days.tagline: Step inside the digital world at 9am. Walk it off through Shinjuku and Shibuya till the neon kicks in.
highlights: 09:00 — TeamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills (tickets confirmed)
12:00 — Saido lunch — vegan kaiseki, no dashi (5 min from teamLab — book it!)
Afternoon — Shinjuku Gyoen + Isetan, Beams Japan, Tokyu Hands
Walk to Shibuya — scramble + Shibuya Sky at golden hour
20:00 — T's Tantan Shibuya, vegan ramen to close the day

transport.note: All within central Tokyo — use Suica

days.food: Saido (Roppongi/Azabudai) — fully vegan kaiseki, no dashi. T's Tantan (Shibuya Station 1F) — vegan ramen, late-night.
days.tip: Wear dark clothing at teamLab — projections look best on black. Saido books up fast on weekends — reserve.

days.title: Kamakura Day Trip
days.tagline: 13th-century capital. The Great Buddha at noon, hydrangeas, then a slow walk along Yuigahama.
highlights: 10:00 — JR Yokosuka Line, Tokyo → Hase (~1h)
12:30 — Kotoku-in: the Daibutsu, 13m of bronze cast in 1252
13:30 — Lunch at Garden House Kamakura (modern menu, easy with diet)
15:00 — Yuigahama Beach walk along the shore
16:30 — Cafe-hopping in Hase, then back to Tokyo by 18:00
days.food: Garden House Kamakura (Yuigahama) — modern menu, easy with diet. Magokoro near the Daibutsu — small vegan cafe.
days.tip: Mid-May = early hydrangeas at Hase-dera. Avoid Sunday afternoon crowds at the Buddha — walk straight from the train.

days.title: Mt Fuji Loop
days.tagline: Pick up the rental at 7:30. Lake reflections at Oishi, Iyashi village, then home before the cloud rolls in.
highlights: 07:30 — Times Car / Toyota Rent pickup in Shinjuku (mid-size, IDP confirmed)
09:30 — Oishi Park, north shore of Lake Kawaguchi — classic Fuji + lake view
11:30 — Kubota Itchiku Art Museum (optional)
13:00 — Lunch at Cafe Troisieme Marche (aesthetic + flexible)
14:30 — Iyashi-no-Sato Nenba — traditional thatched village
19:00 — Back in Shinjuku, pack for Kumamoto
days.food: Konbini stocks before leaving — Fuji-area lunch options are limited. Cafe Troisieme Marche is the safe vegan spot.
days.tip: Clouds roll in by midday almost daily. Hit Oishi Park first while Fuji is still clean. Backup: Cisco Coffee.

days.title: Tokyo → Kumamoto · JAL629
days.tagline: South to Kyushu by lunch. Pick up the kei car at the airport, drop bags, and walk the castle.
highlights: 07:30 — Check out lyf, monorail/limousine to HND
11:50 — JAL629 HND → KMJ (lands 13:35)
14:00 — Nippon Rent-A-Car C08669 pickup (kei car) at KMJ
16:00 — Matsuya Bekkan check-in, drop bags
16:30 — Kumamoto Castle in the late light
18:00 — Dinner at Sakuranobaba Josaien — restaurant village under the castle
days.food: Sakuranobaba Josaien — under-castle restaurant village with multiple options. Veggie izakayas around Kamitori arcade.
days.tip: Kei car on Aso roads will be tight — ask Nippon about an upgrade at the counter if it feels underpowered.

days.title: Aso E-bikes & Kurokawa Onsen
days.tagline: World's largest caldera by morning, a hidden onsen village by afternoon. Three baths on the tegata pass.
highlights: 08:00 — Drive to Mt Aso (kei car, allow extra time on inclines)
09:30 — Naka-dake crater (if open) + Kusasenri grasslands
11:30 — E-bike rental in Aso town — ride around the caldera
15:00 — Kurokawa Onsen, tegata pass = 3 baths for ¥1,500
18:00 — Dinner in Kurokawa, drive back to Kumamoto by ~21:00
days.food: Limited veggie options in Aso area. Print the 'no fish, no dashi' card. Kurokawa kitchens are more accommodating.
days.tip: Tegata pass (¥1,500) lets you bath-hop 3 onsen in Kurokawa. Bring a small towel and tie up long hair.

days.title: Takachiho Gorge — Kayaks
days.tagline: Manai-no-Taki up close — kayak under the waterfall, walk the Gokase path, end at the cave shrine.
highlights: 07:30 — Leave Kumamoto (~2h drive through volcanic highlands)
10:00 — Kayaks under Manai-no-Taki — book at eipro.jp/takachiho1!
11:00 — Local lunch (verify dashi-free options)
12:30 — Gokase walking path along the gorge
14:00 — Amano-Iwato Shrine — the cave where Amaterasu hid
18:00 — Hotel + light dinner in Kumamoto
days.food: Takachiho soba is everywhere — verify it's served without bonito dashi. Bring konbini snacks for the road.
days.tip: Kayak slots disappear fast — book at eipro.jp/takachiho1 the moment they open. Arrive 15 min early.

days.title: Amakusa Islands — Beach Day
days.tagline: Five Bridges out to the islands, white sand at Tomioka, optional dolphins, and one last onsen back home.
highlights: 09:30 — Drive Kumamoto → Amakusa (~1.5h)
11:00 — Cross the Amakusa Five Bridges chain
11:30 — Tomioka or Shimoda beach — turquoise water, almost no tourists
13:00 — Waterside lunch at a port restaurant
15:30 — Optional dolphin-watching cruise (~¥3,000, 1.5h)
20:00 — Onsen at Matsuya + final packing for Osaka
days.food: Port restaurants serve fresh seafood — for veg/GF, supermarket bento is the safer bet. Pack snacks for the beach.
days.tip: Last full day with the kei car. Tomorrow morning is car return + Sakura 752 to Osaka — pack tonight.

days.title: Kumamoto → Osaka · Sakura 752
days.tagline: Return the car at 10:00. Sakura 752 boards at 11:42. Three hours later you're under the Glico sign.
highlights: 09:30 — Check out Matsuya Bekkan
10:00 — Return Nippon car at Kumamoto Station Shinkansen Exit
11:42 — Sakura 752 Kumamoto → Shin-Osaka (3h 17min) · seats 16-CD/17-CD car 4
15:30 — Resol Trinity Osaka check-in
Evening — Dotonbori, first neon experience

activities.name: Return Nippon car at Kumamoto Station
Dotonbori first walk — neon + Glico sign

days.food: First Dotonbori walk is dinner — Optimus Cafe (vegan) on the canal, Tongdam (Thai backup), or Paprika Shokudo Vegan in Umeda.
days.tip: Reservation already includes seats. Pack a snack for the train — most ekiben are fish-based.

days.title: Classic Osaka — Dotonbori & Namba
days.tagline: The motto is kuidaore — eat till you drop. Vintage in Ame-Mura, neons at sundown, Hozenji lanterns at night.
highlights: 12:00 — Lunch at Paprika Shokudo Vegan (Umeda) or Optimus Cafe
14:30 — Namba — Shinsaibashi shopping arcade
16:30 — Dotonbori in daylight, then back at neon
18:00 — America-Mura — vintage shops, cafes
21:00 — Glico Sign + Hozenji Yokocho lantern alley
Pack the overnight bag — Yamato ships Resol → Katsuragi tomorrow morning

activities.name: Lunch — Paprika Shokudo Vegan / Optimus Cafe

transport.note: Recovery day — lots of walking in Namba

days.food: Paprika Shokudo Vegan (Umeda) — book weekend! Optimus Cafe — vegan in Dotonbori. Tongdam — Thai backup.
days.tip: Pack only the daypack you'll need on tomorrow's bike ride. Yamato AM pickup ships your overnight bag to Katsuragi by evening.

days.title: Shimanami 70km · Matsuyama · Dogo Onsen
days.tagline: Six islands by e-bike, then a train across to Shikoku, then 8pm in the Honkan baths. Epic.
highlights: 06:00 — Shinkansen Shin-Osaka → Fukuyama (~1h)
08:00 — Onomichi e-bike pickup, ferry to Mukaishima
11:30 — Setoda lunch on Ikuchi-jima (lemons!)
16:30 — Imabari finish, return bikes
17:00 — Train to Matsuyama (~40 min)
20:00 — Dogo Onsen Honkan (reservation confirmed)
21:30 — Bocchan dango on the Dogo shopping street

activities.name: Ferry to Mukaishima — start the ride

days.food: Setoda lemon stops on Ikuchi-jima. Konbini fuel on Mukaishima/Omishima. Light dinner near Dogo before the 20:00 bath.
days.tip: Daypack only — overnight bag is in Matsuyama already. Padded shorts, gloves, sunglasses. Helmet usually included with rental.

days.title: Naoshima Art Island · Chichu 14:30
days.tagline: Limited Express across to Takamatsu, ferry to Naoshima, Chichu locked in at 14:30. Yellow Pumpkin at golden hour.
highlights: 08:30 — Ishizuchi Limited Express Matsuyama → Takamatsu (~2h 40m)
12:10 — Ferry Takamatsu → Miyanoura (~50 min)
14:30 — Chichu Art Museum (reserved) — Tadao Ando + Turrell + Monet
16:00 — Lee Ufan Museum, then Benesse House
17:30 — Yayoi Kusama Yellow Pumpkin (pier photo)
Evening — ferry Miyanoura → Uno, Shinkansen Okayama → Shin-Osaka
days.food: Benesse Garden Cafe — verify vegan options. Pack snacks for the train back. Late dinner at Resol.
days.tip: Chichu at 14:30 leaves ~3.5h for 3 more sites. Skip Honmura if running late — Pumpkin + Lee Ufan + Benesse are priority. Verify last ferry Miyanoura→Uno.

days.title: Osaka → Tokyo · Cocktail Evening
days.tagline: Slow morning in Osaka. Nozomi north. Last cocktail in Ginza.
highlights: 10:00 — Slow morning, last Osaka impression
12:30 — Check out Resol Trinity
13:30 — Nozomi Shin-Osaka → Tokyo (~2h 30m)
16:00 — Tokyo Station → Sequence Miyashita Park
19:30 — Cocktail bar — Bar High Five (Ginza) / SG Club (Shibuya) / Bar Benfiddich (Shinjuku)

activities.name: Check in at Sequence Miyashita Park

days.food: Bar High Five (Ginza) — old-school perfectionist. SG Club (Shibuya) — modernist split bar. Bar Benfiddich (Shinjuku) — herbal alchemist.
days.tip: Reserve the cocktail bar in advance. Bar High Five doesn't have a sign — it's on the 4th floor of the No.26 building.

days.title: Tokyo Chill Day · Souvenirs
days.tagline: Slow morning, packed bags, last shopping. Save energy for tomorrow.
highlights: Slow morning — coffee + breakfast near hotel
Souvenirs at Don Quijote (cheap), Tokyu Hands (design), Isetan / Mitsukoshi
Pack — Tokyo Station has incredible last-minute omiyage shops
Evening — spontaneous dinner
Sleep early — tomorrow is departure day
days.food: Depachika at Isetan / Mitsukoshi for last-minute treats. Kit-Kats, matcha sweets, senbei (rice crackers — naturally GF).
days.tip: Tax-free kicks in at ¥5,000+ at participating stores — keep your passport handy and don't open sealed items before leaving Japan.

days.title: Departure · LO80 night flight
days.tagline: Drop the bags at NRT in the morning. Spontaneous Tokyo wandering. Then home.
highlights: 09:00 — Check out Sequence
11:00 — NRT baggage drop (LOT allows ~12h before)
12:00 — N'EX back to Tokyo with no luggage
13:30 — Spontaneous wandering, no plan
21:00 — NRT for boarding
22:30 — LO80 Tokyo → Warsaw
days.food: Stock up at NRT — excellent senbei, mochi, regional Kit-Kats. Last konbini coffee before boarding.
days.tip: Alternative: Sagawa / Yamato hotel-to-airport service (~¥2,000–3,000/bag). Saves the morning haul.

japanesePhrases.meaning: I can't eat meat or fish
Do you have tamari soy sauce?

japanesePhrases.japanese: Dashi wa katsuobushi nashi de onegai shimasu
japanesePhrases.meaning: Please make dashi without bonito flakes

safeFoods: Onigiri (rice balls) — umeboshi, kombu, nattō fillings
Mochi — glutinous rice ≠ gluten, naturally GF
watchOut: Soy sauce (shōyu) contains wheat → request tamari
Dashi broth usually made with bonito (fish) → ask for kombu dashi
Miso soup often has bonito dashi

jrPassAnalysis.recommendation: Definitely buy individual tickets. With Tokyo→Kumamoto now a flight, your shinkansen legs are only Kumamoto→Onomichi (¥13,000) and Osaka→Tokyo (¥13,870) plus local trains. The 7-day pass (¥50,000) costs more than your actual train spend. Individual tickets + Nozomi access is the clear winner.
jrPassAnalysis.note: No JR Pass needed. Individual shinkansen tickets can be booked at JR ticket counters (midori no madoguchi) or via SmartEX app.

transport.suicaCard: Buy at airport kiosk. ¥2,000 (¥500 deposit + ¥1,500 balance). Works on all metro, JR local, buses, konbini payments.

takkyubin.what: Luggage forwarding service — send bags between hotels
takkyubin.how: Drop at any konbini (7-Eleven, FamilyMart) or Yamato Transport office

bookings.note: At JR ticket counters (midori no madoguchi)

domesticFlight.note: HND → KMJ one-way (¥8,000–20,000 depending on booking lead time)

trains.note: Shinkansen Kumamoto→Onomichi + Osaka→Tokyo + local trains (no Tokyo→Kumamoto shinkansen)

hotels.note: 14 nights across 5 stays (Kumamoto +1) ÷ 2 people per room

kurokawa.note: Kurokawa Onsen day trip: bus RT ¥5,000 + rotenburo pass ¥1,500 + lunch

amakusa.note: Amakusa day trip: car rental ¥5,000 + dolphin cruise ¥3,000

budget.note: Excludes international flights. Includes domestic HND→KMJ flight. Mid-range estimates. 2 hotel rooms for 4 people.

packing: Light rain jacket — May has sudden showers
Layers — Mt Aso highlands are cooler
Small towel — many restrooms lack hand dryers
Allergy/dietary card in Japanese (print before trip)
Minimal luggage — lots of stairs and tight trains
Coin purse — Japan uses more coins than expected

travels.details: WAW 22:50 → NRT ~16:20 next day. Then N'EX to Shinjuku.
Day trip. Return via JR same evening.
Pickup 7:30 in Shinjuku. Loop the lake, return by 19:00.
HND 11:50 → KMJ 13:35. Nippon kei car C08669 ready at 14:00.
Aso crater + Kusasenri, e-bike caldera, then Kurokawa onsen tegata.
Manai-no-Taki kayaks at 10:00. Gokase walking path. Amano-Iwato.
Five Bridges, Tomioka beach, optional dolphin cruise.
Shinkansen → local → ferry → ride 6 islands → train across to Matsuyama by 18:00.
Matsuyama → Takamatsu → Naoshima art island → Uno → Shinkansen back.
Nozomi — fastest bullet train. Mt Fuji from the right side if lucky.
NRT 22:30. Sleep in the air. Land in Warsaw morning.

hotels.budget: Up to €250/night per room (2 rooms needed)
hotels.note: Prices are approximate per room per night in May 2026. Book early for best rates. All hotels can receive takkyubin luggage.

restaurants.note: Curated for vegetarian/vegan travelers with celiac-level gluten allergy. GF = gluten-free. Always carry a Japanese allergy card and tamari packets.
restaurants.allergyCardJp: 私はセリアック病です。小麦・大麦・ライ麦を食べられません。醤油の代わりにたまりを使ってください。
restaurants.allergyCardEn: I have celiac disease. I cannot eat wheat, barley, or rye. Please use tamari instead of soy sauce.
safeFoods: Onigiri — umeboshi, kombu, nattō fillings (check labels for wheat)
Yakiimo — roasted sweet potato from street vendors
Fresh fruit — Japan's fruit is extraordinary
Tofu (hiyayakko/yudofu) — ask for tamari instead of soy sauce
dangerFoods: Soy sauce (shōyu) — contains wheat. Request tamari.
Ramen/udon/soba noodles — wheat (soba is buckwheat + wheat mix)
Dashi broth — usually bonito (fish), ask for kombu dashi
Okonomiyaki — wheat batter unless rice flour specified

Onsen ryokan recommended — full Hakone experience
Gateway to Japanese Alps and Nakasendo trail

days.title: Nara Day Trip
days.tagline: Ancient capital, giant Buddha, sacred deer. The day trip that got its own day.
days.splitNote: Jacek + Ola take the Shinkansen to Tokyo this morning. You stay in Osaka and head to Nara.
highlights: JR Namba → Nara — 45 min, ¥580
Tōdai-ji — the world's largest wooden building, housing a 15m bronze Buddha
Nara Park — over 1,200 free-roaming deer, sacred messengers of the gods
Kōfuku-ji — five-story pagoda, one of Japan's oldest temple complexes
Kasuga-taisha shrine — 3,000 stone lanterns lining the approach
Return to Osaka for evening

activities.name: Say goodbye to Jacek + Ola at Osaka station

days.food: Nara has more GF options than you'd expect. Look for mochi (rice-based, GF), kaki no ha sushi (persimmon leaf sushi — skip the soy sauce or use your tamari). Avoid anything with dashi broth unless you confirm it's kombu-only.
days.tip: Deer biscuits (shika senbei, ¥200) are sold at stalls everywhere. The deer know how to bow — if you bow first, they bow back. Don't tease them though, they WILL headbutt you.

days.title: Osaka → Kyoto — Higashiyama
days.tagline: Trading neon for tradition. Three days in Japan's cultural heart.
highlights: JR Special Rapid to Kyoto — 30 min, ¥580
Kiyomizu-dera — iconic wooden terrace with panoramic views
Ninenzaka → Sannenzaka — traditional streets with pagoda views
Hōkan-ji Temple — the five-story pagoda from every Kyoto photo
Philosopher's Path — 2km canal walk lined with cherry trees and temples
Higashiyama Jisho-ji (Silver Pavilion) — the understated counterpart to Kinkaku-ji

activities.name: Check out Osaka hotel, JR to Kyoto
Drop bags at Kyoto hotel (or use coin locker at station)

days.food: CHOICE (Higashiyama) — 100% vegan AND 100% gluten-free restaurant. Ramen, burgers, cakes — all safe. Gion Soy Milk Ramen — only dedicated GF ramen shop in Japan, rice noodles, celiac-certified.
days.tip: Kiyomizu-dera before 9am is magical. The wooden terrace juts out over a hillside — no nails, just interlocking beams. Sunset from here is extraordinary.

days.title: Kyoto — Mountain Temples & Markets
days.tagline: Hike between mountain temples, then hunt for treasures at Nishiki Market.
highlights: Kurama-Kibune mountain hike — 2-3 hrs through ancient forest
Kuramadera Temple at the start, Kifune Shrine at the finish
Lunch at Yoshuji — shōjin ryōri (Buddhist cuisine) in a farmhouse with fire pit
Afternoon: Nishiki Market — 400m of food stalls, Kyoto's kitchen
Nijo Castle — Tokugawa shogunate seat, famous 'nightingale floors'
Kyoto International Manga Museum if time permits

activities.name: Eizan Line back to central Kyoto
Dinner — Moon and Back Ramen (near Nishiki)

transport.note: Eizan Line from Demachiyanagi to Kurama/Kibune

days.food: Yoshuji (Kurama) — Buddhist vegetarian in a traditional farmhouse. Mostly naturally GF, English menu. Moon and Back Ramen — vegan ramen near Nishiki, GF rice noodles available (+¥275).
days.tip: The Kurama-Kibune trail is moderate but has some steep sections and exposed tree roots (the famous kinonesandō). Wear proper shoes. The hike is easier Kurama → Kibune (net downhill to the shrine).

days.title: Kyoto — Moss, Gold & Geisha
days.tagline: The temples the day-trippers never reach. Plus Gion at its most atmospheric.
highlights: Saihō-ji (Koke-dera) — the legendary moss temple, 130 species of moss
Mandatory sutra-copying meditation, then garden stroll
Sanjūsangendō — 1,001 life-size golden Kannon statues in one hall
Tōfuku-ji — massive Zen temple, autumn maple garden
Gion evening stroll — deeper into geisha culture than the day trip allowed

transport.note: Bus to Saihō-ji (Kokedera-Suzumushidera-mae stop), then city buses

days.food: TOUSUIRO Gion — GF kaiseki in a 130-year-old merchant house. ¥7,500 for the vegan 'Rokuhara' course. Book 3 days ahead for GF preparation.
days.tip: Saihō-ji REQUIRES advance reservation (2 months ahead, max 2 per booking). You'll copy Buddhist sutras in ink before seeing the garden — embrace it, it's incredibly meditative. The moss garden is worth every yen.
bookAhead: Saihō-ji (Koke-dera) — book at saihoji-kokedera.com, ¥4,000 + ¥110 fee, max 2 per booking

days.title: Kyoto → Hakone
days.tagline: Bullet train east, then hot springs in the mountains. Buy the Hakone Free Pass.
highlights: Shinkansen Kyoto → Odawara — 2 hrs
Buy Hakone Free Pass at Odawara (¥6,000/2 days — covers everything)
Hakone Tozan Railway up the mountain switchbacks
Settle into ryokan/hotel — onsen time!
Evening: first onsen experience. Remember: wash first, then soak. No swimwear.

activities.name: Buy Hakone Free Pass at Odawara Station
Ryokan dinner (if included) or Shika-jaya (tofu dishes)

transport.note: Hakone Free Pass (¥6,000) covers all transport within Hakone for 2 days

days.food: Shika-jaya — traditional tofu/yamaimo dishes near Hakone-Yumoto, vegan Okabe Zen course. Nukafuku (Gora) — 100% GF rice bran donuts, vegan sausages, smoothies. Staff speaks English and knows about celiac.
days.tip: Hakone Free Pass is ESSENTIAL — covers trains, cable car, ropeway, boat, and buses for 2 days. Buy at Odawara.

rules: Wash COMPLETELY before entering the bath — use the small stools and buckets at the shower area
Enter fully naked — no swimwear allowed
Keep your small towel out of the water (fold it on your head)
Be quiet — onsens are for peaceful relaxation
If you have tattoos: ask first, but Hakone is generally more lenient than cities
onsenEtiquette.tip: Private baths (kashikiri) are available at most ryokan — perfect if you're nervous about communal bathing

days.title: Hakone — Hiking & Hot Springs
days.tagline: Volcanic valleys, sacred lakes, and the old Tokaido highway through cedar forests.
highlights: Old Tokaido Road hike — ancient cedar-lined stone path, 2-3 hrs
Owakudani — steaming volcanic valley, black eggs, sulphur vents
Hakone Ropeway over the caldera — spectacular views
Lake Ashi boat cruise — Mt Fuji reflected in the water (if clear)
Hakone Shrine & Kuzuryū Shrine — torii gate on the lake
Amasake Tea House — 400-year-old rest stop on the old highway

transport.note: All covered: ropeway, cable car, boat, buses

days.food: Amasake Tea House — 400-year-old thatched-roof stop on the Tokaido Road. Serves amazake (sweet fermented rice drink, naturally GF and vegan). The black eggs at Owakudani are NOT vegetarian (they're eggs). Pack snacks for the hike.
days.tip: Start the Tokaido Road hike early — the cedar avenue in morning light is magical. Take the bus to Hatajuku to skip the boring road section. Owakudani may close if volcanic activity increases — check on the day.

days.title: Hakone → Matsumoto
days.tagline: From volcanic hot springs to samurai castle. The Japanese Alps are calling.
highlights: Train Hakone-Yumoto → Odawara → Shinjuku → Matsumoto — ~4 hrs
Matsumoto Castle — Japan's oldest five-tier castle, a National Treasure
Nawate-dōri shopping street — retro frog-themed lane along the river
Evening: soba noodles — Matsumoto's specialty (buckwheat = naturally GF!)

activities.name: Arrive Matsumoto, check into hotel, lunch

days.food: Takagi Soba — 100% buckwheat soba noodles (naturally GF). Near the castle. They're very knowledgeable about gluten. Asian Station — Nepalese/Indian, vegan curries, extremely dietary-friendly, #8 rated in Matsumoto. Book ahead, small restaurant.
days.tip: Matsumoto Castle is Japan's oldest five-tiered castle. The stairs inside are STEEP — almost ladders. It's worth climbing to the top for the mountain views. Arrive before 3pm to avoid the rush.

days.title: Nakasendo Trail — Magome to Tsumago
days.tagline: Walk the 400-year-old postal road through mountain forests. Edo-period Japan, preserved.
days.stay: Matsumoto hotel (or overnight in Tsumago for full immersion)

Hike the Nakasendo trail: Magome → Tsumago — 8 km, 2-3 hrs

transport.note: Bus to Magome, hike to Tsumago, bus+train back to Matsumoto

days.food: Pack snacks before leaving! On the trail: Tateba-jaya serves free matcha at the midpoint. In Tsumago: gohei mochi — grilled rice dumplings with sesame/walnut sauce, naturally GF and vegan (confirm no fish broth). Tawaraya and Yoshimuraya in Tsumago for soba.
days.tip: Walk Magome → Tsumago (not the reverse) — it's net downhill after the pass. The cobblestones are VERY slippery when wet, bring proper hiking shoes. Send your big luggage ahead via coin lockers or takkyubin. This is one of Japan's most beautiful walks — take your time.

nakasendoTrail.terrain: Cobblestone paths, forest trails, some steep sections
whatToPack: Sturdy hiking shoes (cobblestones slippery when wet)
Snacks from konbini (onigiri, edamame, fruit, rice crackers)

restaurants.note: Extra restaurant recommendations for extended trip locations. The couple has celiac-level gluten allergy — GF safety is critical. They're less experienced with Japan, so detailed guidance matters more.

spots.name: CHOICE
spots.mustTry: Everything — 100% vegan AND 100% gluten-free establishment. Ramen, burgers, cakes, all safe.
spots.note: Entirely dedicated vegan/GF restaurant. 32 seats. Closed Thursdays.

spots.name: Gion Soy Milk Ramen
spots.mustTry: Soy milk ramen with rice noodles — the only dedicated GF ramen restaurant in Japan
spots.note: Celiac-certified. Also has GF gyoza, curry rice, and vegan cakes. 11:00-20:30 daily.

spots.name: TOUSUIRO Gion
spots.mustTry: Vegan kaiseki 'Rokuhara' course (¥7,500) — multi-course Japanese haute cuisine in a 130-year-old merchant house
spots.note: Requires advance reservation (3 days for GF preparation). A once-in-a-lifetime meal.

spots.name: Moon and Back Ramen Bar
spots.mustTry: Spicy Tandan Ramen — white sesame broth with bok choy and tofu skin
spots.note: GF rice noodles available (+¥275 surcharge). Two Kyoto locations.

spots.name: Yoshuji
spots.mustTry: Vegetarian noodle bowls and set lunch in a traditional farmhouse with irori fire pit
spots.note: 3 min from Kurama Station. English menu. Mostly naturally GF. Closed Tuesdays. Call ahead to confirm GF.

hakone.label: Hakone

spots.name: Nukafuku
spots.mustTry: Rice bran donuts — rotating daily flavors, all 100% GF
spots.note: Owner speaks excellent English and understands celiac. Also has vegan sausages, smoothies, dango. Takeaway only.

spots.name: Shika-jaya
spots.mustTry: Okabe Zen course — fully vegan tofu set
spots.note: Bring your own tamari — standard soy sauce has wheat. Staff experienced with modifications. Closed Thursdays.

hakone.survivalTips: Hakone is tough for GF. Most restaurants use standard soy sauce and dashi. Your best bets: Nukafuku (100% GF, Gora area), ryokan meals (request GF 2+ weeks ahead), and konbini onigiri. Pack tamari packets and GF snacks from Kyoto before arriving. The Amasake Tea House on the Old Tokaido Road serves amazake (fermented rice drink) which is naturally GF and vegan.

matsumoto.label: Matsumoto & Nakasendo

spots.name: Takagi Soba
spots.mustTry: Juwari soba (100% buckwheat noodles) — naturally GF. Request plain or with salt instead of soy sauce.
spots.note: Buckwheat is NOT wheat — it's naturally gluten-free. This shop uses 100% buckwheat, no wheat filler. Staff very knowledgeable.

spots.name: Asian Station
spots.nameJp: アジアンステーション
spots.mustTry: Vegan curry with rice — naturally GF. Excellent naan but skip it (wheat).
spots.note: #8 of 998 restaurants on TripAdvisor, 4.9 rating. Only a few tables — book ahead. Owner very allergy-aware.

spots.name: Menshoshinbusakiya
spots.nameJp: 麺小新ぶさきや 松本店
spots.mustTry: Vegan ramen with brown rice noodles — specifically designed for celiac diners
spots.note: Staff extremely knowledgeable about celiac disease. Small chain with 4 locations in Japan.

matsumoto.survivalTips: Matsumoto is surprisingly good for GF because of its soba culture — 100% buckwheat (juwari) soba is naturally GF. Always confirm 'juwari' (十割) not 'nihachi' (二八, which is 80% buckwheat + 20% wheat). On the Nakasendo trail: pack ALL food from konbini before starting. The only trail stop is Tateba-jaya which offers free matcha (GF). In Tsumago: gohei mochi (grilled rice on a stick with sesame/walnut sauce) is naturally GF and vegan — confirm no fish broth.

forLessExperienced: Always carry your allergy card (allergyCardJp from the main restaurants section) — show it to every restaurant
Download HappyCow and FindMeGlutenFree apps before leaving
Google Translate camera mode — point your phone at any menu for instant translation
7-Eleven ATMs give the best exchange rate and have English menus
IC card (Suica/Pasmo) works on ALL trains, metros, buses, and in konbini
Konbini onigiri (rice balls) are your emergency food — umeboshi, kombu, natto fillings are GF and vegan
Japan runs on cash more than you'd expect — always have ¥10,000+ on you
Trains run EXACTLY on time. If the schedule says 10:32, it leaves at 10:32.
Bow when someone bows to you. Say 'sumimasen' (excuse me) and 'arigatou gozaimasu' (thank you)
Shoes off in temples, ryokans, and many restaurants — wear socks without holes
emergencyFood: 7-Eleven: onigiri (rice balls), edamame, plain rice, fruit, salad
FamilyMart: GF rice crackers (senbei), mochi, banana, boiled eggs
Lawson: yakiimo (roasted sweet potato) in season, fruit cups
Any supermarket after 7pm: bento boxes 30-50% off — look for rice-based ones
practicalTips.jrPassNote: With the extended route (Kyoto → Hakone → Matsumoto → Tokyo), buying a 7-day JR Pass (¥50,000) might actually make sense for the extended couple. Their shinkansen Kyoto→Odawara alone is ¥11,000, plus trains to Matsumoto (¥6,620) and local trains. Calculate before buying.
